value.body: A two-year Master of Physiotherapy (MPT) after a BPT. You specialise in one area — commonly musculoskeletal/orthopaedics, neurology, cardio-respiratory, sports, paediatrics or community physiotherapy — with supervised clinical work and a dissertation. Physiotherapy is a recognised profession under the National Commission for Allied and Healthcare Professions Act, 2021.

items.label: Course length
items.note: 4 semesters with clinical postings and a dissertation

value.title: How you get in
value.body: A BPT with internship completed, usually with a minimum percentage. Admission is through university or state entrance tests, institute tests, or merit, depending on the state and university.

value.title: At a glance
items: An MPT is the usual requirement for teaching posts in physiotherapy colleges.
Specialisation helps in hospitals, sports teams and rehabilitation centres, but many clinics value hands-on experience as much as the degree.
Private-college fees vary widely; government seats are limited.
Some graduates set up their own practice after a few years of experience.
